CoFoPo and the liberal menace

How can a whale be harpooned, if it never surfaces?

The CoFoPo – short for Cohesive Force Power – is a nation with blurred borders, a continent in motion from west to east. At least, according to the Unionists.

To the now-defunct Committee of Regulators, however, it is an inter-feudal alliance made up of 57 Stain Fiefdoms – republics guilty of state conglomeration. The productive incapacity of the smaller fiefs had become a sinister banner of the past, a liberal hemorrhage threatening to drag us back two hundred cycles.

Had the Committee of Regulators not been overthrown for greed and individualism, none of this would have ever happened.
Death To Privatisation

You there! By Juno’s breast!

If you care for our industry, stop while you still can! With this, you seek only to benefit the bastard sons of Confeudocratism! You forget, with this disgraceful move, the boon the New Youth once brought to Lundonstoch.

Every liberal concession makes us less united, less like comrades.
To tax private interests less today is to set a precedent for the cycles to come.
Denationalization and Decentralization VOL.3

Charles of Gheudogal founded the first Fief of the Globe, the embryo of civilization, nestled among the lush hills that would one day be known as the D’Oilands – the Nation of God.

In the 1460th cycle, his son, Pepin of Charles, carried forward the social upheaval begun by his father; not through speeches or decrees, but by devouring the surrounding villages. Thus, the Fief swelled, outgrew the bounds of its cradle, and soon became a City without horizon: the first true kingdom of the Middle Moore.

We all know how cities work: they are never sated. Their hunger is eternal. They grow like Pitch Black spreading through the body, corrupting the entire apparat from within. By the 1600th cycle, the entire Middle Moore – the central island dividing the western and eastern flanks of the Globe – had been nearly consumed by the Empire of D’Oil, the chosen people of Djesok.
Denationalization and Decentralization VOL.6

One arc after the death of King Theodogald, the Army of Altomare launched the invasion of the D’Oilan Kingdom. The Three-Winds Campaign pursued a triple goal: to colonize the Middle Moore, the Northern Beacon, and the Southern Kurs Lands.

The Middle Moore became a colony within three arcs – with the exception of the barbarian regions of Loondvohn and Eckymbourough, where King Emilio Quinto met the same fierce resistance that had once halted Pepin, Theodogald, and the army of D’Oil.

The campaign in the Kurs Lands was a success: in just two cycles, Altomare could count on the enslavement of the entire southeastern continent. The Northern Beacon’s Campaign, however, never even began – the entire fleet veered off course and found itself in the Western Continent: pure, untouched, never defiled by the hand of civilized man.

Ten thousand men set sail from the Kingdom of Altomare... and never returned.
Denationalization and Decentralization VOL.7

In the 1640th cycle, 80% of the Middle Moore was under the control of Altomare’s occupation forces, with the fiefs of Loondvohn and Eckymbourough standing as the last bastions of resistance. Meanwhile, in the occupied Kingdom of D’Oil, the absence of a monarch for over 40 cycles had sparked a popular-religious movement that saw in Merge of Levellier the long-awaited answer to the invaders.

The Holy Revolution saw thousands of D’Oilans rise up against the oppressor, marching under the rediscovered banner of the Surviving God, Djesok. Altomare’s occupying forces soon found themselves fighting on three separate fronts.

By the 1644th cycle, the army of Altomare had been expelled from the island for good, and Merge of Levellier became the Savior of the Middle Moore, earning the title of OberMan of D’Oil – the first leadership role in global society ever to be chosen by the people.

Not long after, the D’Oilans witnessed the birth of two neighboring nations: Boldenisle and Skutyard.

The crowns were shattered by the elected OberMen.
Denationalization and Decentralization VOL.11

At the dusk of the Vigorous Epoch, one last war struck the Middle Moore: the Holy War.

Truthfully, the reasons behind it were rather absurd. During the 100th Festival of Liberation from Altomare, OberMan Jacque of Stromae – with the blessing of the Djesokite Vicar of D’Oil, Remì of Djesok – invited the OberMen of the two historic rival nations, Boldenisle and Skutyard, to witness the Holy Parade as a gesture of peace and goodwill.

A week after the invitations were sent, two wicker parcels with silver tags were delivered to the gates of the Golden Manor of the D’Oilan ruler. When Jacque opened them, he found the worst of indignities: two pieces of solidified shit.

The darker one bore the signature of Lundonstoch. The grayish one was marked by Eggmouth.
The Vessel of Devereux

After all these cycles, I found her unrecognizable — worn down, abandoned to the injuries of time. How could I have left behind such an essential part of my very being?

The keel was lost, shattered beyond repair. And yet, there was still grace in her bent form, dignity in her ribs of balbo and iron. In her I saw not an end, but the beginning of a rebirth.
A new perspective: to ennoble decay, to redeem ruin.

I rebuilt her in her own image. The same ribs, yes — but a new heart, forged not from vanity, but from memory. And with horror, I realized the sea beneath her was still the same as before.
Devereux: the Missed Regret

It was snowing, and yet the sky was made of wood.
The Professor raised his sword – still wet with the tyrant’s blood – toward the Thesis, and solemnly gathered the ashes of his fallen companions: Polyanna and Fitzroy.

Outside a window far too small to frame the horizon, the crowd cheered the corpse of the last president.
Ermak Panin: The First Revolutionary

"The right of peoples to self-determination includes the right to their own state. However, the founding of a state does not increase a people’s freedom."

Ermak opens his book Feudocratic Thought of the 1806th cycle with these words, unaware that, just a few cycles later, he would inspire a global revolution.
Faded Comrades

What defines a Lundoneer? 

What virtues shape OUR model citizen? 

What would they give their life for? 

Reader, if these questions find no answer within you, then you are a victim of the cultural fading that plagues our Fiefdom.
Our comrades must reclaim discipline, method, and action.

We do not need new soils — we need a return to our roots!

Monromano murder at the dusk of the thesis

The bodies were laid out in a row.

Twas impossible for me to determine the time of death — the snow must have preserved them for days, if not quints, before the Border DCB found them.

“May Djesok protect you, inspector Monromano,” came the thick D’Oilan-accented voice of that clean-faced Enguerran.

I looked at him. Calling him a “comrade” would’ve been a stretch.
Moors in uniform

After all those cycles, Leofwine no longer knew whether it was Edwin’s stubbornness that had made him fall in love, or just his stupid, good-natured hard-headedness.
What he did know, with certainty, was that he would have given anything to see his comrade’s white smile again – rather than those crimson, shattered teeth.

With every blow from the Gappers, something of him vanished; there was no trace left of his nose.
Io Prossimo – Burdensome Philosophy

Once, I was convinced that my existence concealed a deeper principle – an immutable and secret core lying at the heart of my being. Such belief held me captive, like a faint flame encased in a glass lantern, through which the Globe spun around me in ever more frantic motion, dragging me toward a dark and inescapable end.

But there came a day – perhaps by revelation, or weariness – when that illusion shattered.
The invisible walls dissolved like mist before the light of the Thesis, and I understood that there was no core, no fixed “self” to guard or fear.

Since then, no longer channeled along a path decreed by Gods I do not know, I walk in the open air of being– like one who, waking from a long dream, finds themselves at last a part of the moore, no longer a spectator behind glass.
LMA REFERENDUM – Invitation to Green Citizens

Citizens with Green Passfief, we need your help: with this missive, we officially announce the start of voting for the LMA popular referendum.

A ‘yes’ vote guarantees military equipment for the defense of the inner districts, while a ‘no’ vote guarantees the maintenance of the current state. The Great Feudal Council promises not to influence a choice that belongs solely and exclusively to the people.

Remember that DCB vassals will come to collect your ballots in five days.
Happy democracy to ye all!
T-Based – Between OLD and NEW WAVE

Melancholy turned into joy — an act of resistance against the Hollow Gap. If the Old Wave embodied passive acceptance of death, the New Wave rejects anything that cannot be celebrated or lived through one's own skin. More than that: it is a form of education. A reclaiming of collective identity meant to transcend death.
The Lundoneer - 21 Polymonath of the 2028th Cycle

From White Vessel to Edith, the murmurs of the people have finally been heard; today the DCB will enter the dormitories and deliver the ballots into your hands. Remember, a vote for ‘Yes’ is a vote for security and the deployment of military weaponry in the inner districts, so that no one else falls like Lundocks!
The Lundoneer - 33 Polymonath of the 2028th Cycle

YES! YES! YES! YES! YES!

The people have spoken, the ‘Yes’ wins with over 73%!

The Burgrave of Wynnstan, Tardis, announces to the Kinejournal the overwhelming victory:
“A united people is a strong fief. This victory proves the strength of the feudocratic collective and fiercely rejects the liberal CoFoPo threat!”
The Second Coming of Djesok

During the final days of the 1422nd cycle, the people of D’Oil found no peace.
The sudden appearance of a burning globe in the sky disturbed their rest; night was lit as day, and a constant hum rendered all daily activity impossible.
Barricaded in their shacks, they awaited the return of Charles of Gheudogal, who had ventured to the hill, eager to observe and understand the strange phenomenon.

Days passed, and there was no word of Charles. Many presumed him dead.
A quint went by, then an arc; eventually, an entire cycle.
The globe burned on, unmoving in the sky like a watchful eye, and unrest spread among the people – until, suddenly, its light vanished, and true night fell once more.

Then, from the hill, two figures descended to meet the gathered crowd.
One was their leader, but his face had changed. New muscles adorned his jaw.
The other lacked any distinct features, and yet its face reflected all that stood before it; it seemed not to touch the ground as it walked.

Fear took hold of the people. Tension swelled. From the crowd, someone hurled a stone at the faceless figure – but it struck Charles instead, wounding him in the eye.
Unshaken, the ruler placed a hand upon his heart and began to sing a melody of comfort – he sang in sound and meaning, in the newborn tongue of D’Oil, of the "Second Coming of Djesok," the God Whose Face Reflects – the God who survived the Silent Epoch.

Scholars of the Cunning Epoch claim that thus the people of D’Oil learned their language – in a single night, dancing around their leader and some random God.

Needless to say, the violent farmer was later drowned in a puddle of mud.
The Lundoneer - 36 Jumonath of the 2028th Cycle

Bathed in the first rays of the Thesis, the Great Feudal Council, gathered in Newborne, announces on the Kinejournal microphones that Lundonstoch is in lockdown. Following the CoFoPo claim of the dramatic disappearance of Margrave Aldred, Lundonstoch shows its iron fist and deploys a massive DCB contingent in Lundocks.

From today until further notice, all feudal and privatized activities are closed, and citizens are required to remain in their dormitories. Wages for all feudal workers will continue uninterrupted: enjoy your early vacation!
Undercover the Percivals

My name is Ella, I come from the district of Edith, and I was embedded within the Percival Consortium for over three cycles, during the transition between the Fifth and Sixth leaderships.

First of all, let me say this: the legends aren’t true.
They’re not a criminal organization made up of brothers, sisters, and cousins who all share the same name. ‘Percival’ is a name one must earn – a noble title within a society that stands outside feudal law.

I was once a Percival.
This is the story of how I managed to bring down seven brothers in what would later be known as The Great Fitzmonath Raid.
